title: Snatch
events_chronological: Franky Four Fingers and his crew rob an Antwerp diamond house dressed as Hasidic Jews and walk out with an eighty-four carat stone.
Doug the Head's cousin Avi tells Franky from New York to bring the stone straight over.
Boris the Blade tells Franky about a bookmaker's in London and simultaneously tips off the pawnbrokers Sol and Vinny to rob him there.
Boxing promoters Turkish and Tommy send Gorgeous George to buy a caravan from a camp of Irish Travellers.
The bare-knuckle fighter Mickey O'Neil knocks George out over the deal, leaving Turkish without a fighter for Brick Top's fixed bout.
Turkish has to put Mickey in the fight instead, and promises Brick Top that Mickey will go down in the fourth round.
Franky lands in London, delivers the stone to Doug, and heads for the bookmaker's to bet on the fight.
Sol, Vinny and Tyrone bungle the robbery, take Franky's arm and his case, and are chased off by Boris.
Mickey knocks his opponent out cold in the first round, and Brick Top loses a fortune and takes it out on Turkish.
Avi flies in from New York, finds Franky gone, and hires the bounty hunter Bullet-Tooth Tony to find him.
Boris takes Franky, cuts off his arm to get the case open, and finds that the stone is not inside it.
Tony traces the pawnbrokers, shoots their car to pieces and takes both them and the stone.
Brick Top feeds Franky to his pigs and tells Turkish and Tommy what will happen to them if the second fight goes wrong.
Turkish and Tommy tell Mickey to go down in the fourth, and Brick Top's men burn Mickey's mother to death in her caravan.
Boris ambushes Tony's car with Sol and Vinny inside, and in the shootout Tony, Boris and Vinny are all killed.
Tyrone gets away with the dog that has swallowed the diamond.
Mickey knocks his opponent out again in the fourth round, and the Travellers massacre Brick Top's men in the crowd.
Turkish and Tommy find Brick Top and shoot him, and by morning the Travellers have vanished.
The dog is handed in at a pet shop, coughs up the diamond, and Turkish and Tommy end up holding it.
syuzhet_notes: Turkish narrates in retrospect and introduces characters with freeze-frames and captions at the moment they become useful rather than when they first appear, so the film jumps sideways between three largely simultaneous strands - the diamond, the fights, the pawnbrokers. Told-order bullets 4 and 6 drop back to set up men already on screen, and bullet 8 shows the fight that the robbery at bullet 9 was timed to coincide with.
fabula_notes: The three strands overlap heavily and the film supplies no dates, so the ordering rests on its two fixed points - the two fights - and on who is holding the stone at any moment. Franky's fate and the dog's route to the pet shop are both established after the fact rather than shown in sequence.
